label: Ubiquiti FiberPoE Gen2
description: Outdoor optical-to-PoE transport: one 1 Gbps SFP cage, one GbE PoE output port and a DC terminal block, 16-57V DC in.
notes: Vendor figures from the Ubiquiti tech specs page: Networking interface **(1) 1 Gbps SFP port**, **(1) GbE PoE port (10/100 MbE not supported)**, DC terminal block and DC RJ45 injection, input **16-57V DC**, output 24V or 50V DC 2-wire. **The PoE port refuses 10/100 devices** - it is gigabit-only - which is the single detail that breaks an install built around an older airMAX CPE. The DC terminal block and DC RJ45 injection are recorded in these notes rather than as interfaces: the catalogue models data ports, and a 2-wire DC input is not one - it is the power feed, 16-57 V DC in with 24 V or 50 V DC out.

poe.note: The FiberPoE Gen2 makes no power of its own: it injects DC arriving on its terminal block or DC-in RJ45 port onto the PoE port, and Ubiquiti's tech-spec table says so in the vendor's own word - 'Power Method: DC Terminal Block, 2-Wire, 24V DC/50 VDC / DC in RJ45 Port, 2-pair (4, 5+; 7, 8-) (24V DC input), or 4-pair (24V DC/50V DC input) passthrough / PoE RJ45 port, 2-pair (4, 5+; 7, 8-) (24V DC input), or 4-pair (24V DC/50V DC input) PoE passthrough' (https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/fiber/optical-data-transport-for-outdoor-poe-devices, HTTP 200, 587,458 B, read 2026-11-24). No wattage is printed for the PoE output; the page's only power figures are 'Input DC voltage: 16-57V', 'DC Output: Terminal block, 24V DC/50V DC, 2-wire' and 'Power Consumption: 1.5W (Typical)', none of which is a PSE ceiling.
